p0.original: 第三章 感觉与知觉

p1.en: Translator of this chapter: Jin Woo Ming

p3.original: 本章视频导读，请扫描二维码观看。
p3.en: Scan the QR code to watch the video introduction to this chapter.

p4.original: 感觉与知觉是我们与外部物质世界联系的大门。
p4.en: Feelings and consciousness are our gateway to the outside material world.

p5.original: 感觉系统让我们可以感受物体的单一属性，通过看、听、嗅、吃、摸等与外界交互，并在交互中感知世界，形成我们的视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉等感受。感觉有多重要呢？我们可以反过来想一下，如果完全看不到（听不到、闻不到……）会怎么样？这样大家就彻底理解了。即使是大家避之唯恐不及的痛觉，也有它的用处，它至少可以让我们远离危险。
p5.en: The sensory system allows us to feel the single properties of objects, interact with the outside world by seeing, hearing, sniffing, eating, touching, and in interactively sense the world, forming our vision, hearing, smell, taste, touch, etc. How important does it feel? We can think of the other way around. What happens if we don't see it at all? So we all get it. Even the sense of fear that everyone has avoided, it has its usefulness, at least to keep us from danger.

p6.original: 但话说回来，感觉的结果并不是那么泾渭分明的。“江流天地外，山色有无中”这样的感受是完全正常的。本章的感觉阈限和信号检测论等内容会帮助我们理解那些“依稀仿佛”的感觉。
p6.en: But then again, the results are not so clear. It is perfectly normal to feel the same way that "the mountains are in the air and out of the sky." The sense thresholds and the signal detection theory in this chapter will help us understand the senses of “similarity”.

p7.original: 知觉则侧重于理解物体的整体属性，还受我们的知识和经验的影响。即使我们想保持冷静，尽量客观地观察这个世界，但最终的观察结果仍会不可避免地被打上我们个人的烙印。从出生开始，我们就逐渐戴上了个性化的有色眼镜（助听器……），而且一旦戴上就几乎终生无法取下来。
p7.en: The perception focuses on understanding the overall attributes of the object and is influenced by our knowledge and experience. Even if we want to remain calm and to observe the world as objectively as possible, the final observations will inevitably be branded on us personally. From birth, we have gradually worn individual coloured glasses (heart aid...) and once they are worn, they are almost never taken off.

p8.original: 那么，问题就来了。我们每个人看到的、听到的都一样吗？值得庆幸的是，大多数人的感觉都是相似的，因此我们可以彼此交流我们在这个五光十色的世界的体验。但是个体差异总是存在的。所以同一种味道，有人说是酸的，有人说是甜的。同一种颜色，有人说是蓝的，有人说是绿的。
p8.en: So, the problem is there. Is everything we see and hear the same? Fortunately, most people feel the same way, so we can share our experiences in this light and light world. But individual differences always exist. So the same smell, some say sour, others say sweet. The same color, some say blue, others say green.

p9.original: 也许有人已经发现，如果说知识和经验影响知觉，那么假设能影响和操纵其他人的知识和经验，这不就意味着能影响和操纵别人的知觉吗？本章的阈下知觉部分将讨论这方面的有趣内容。
p9.en: Perhaps one has found that if knowledge and experience affect perception, then assuming that knowledge and experience of others can be influenced and manipulated, does that mean that perception of others can be influenced and manipulated? Interesting elements in this regard will be discussed in the sensory section below the threshold of this chapter.

p10.original: 在这一章里，我们还能学到很多有关感知觉的心理学知识，包括各个感觉系统的工作机理，影响感知觉的各种因素。大家如果想尽快了解，可以先浏览本章最后的小结部分，在这里就不一一赘述了。
p10.en: In this chapter, we can also learn a great deal about sensory psychology, including the working mechanisms of the various sensory systems, and the factors that influence sensory. If you want to know as soon as possible, you can look at the last subsection of this chapter, and we will not dwell on it here.

p11.original: 最后，感恩我们的感官系统和我们的大脑，让我们的生活有声有色，多姿多彩！
p11.en: Finally, thanks to our sensory system and our brains, our lives are colorful and colorful!

p14.original: 克劳德·莫奈（Claude Monet）的《罂粟花田》（Coquelicots）的闪烁效果源于视觉系统的一个奇妙特性，这一章将对此做出解释。
p14.en: The scintillation effect of Claude Monnet's Coquelicots stems from a fantastic feature of the visual system, which will be explained in this chapter.
